headline: Bruins and Celtics take over the Garden for massive Friday doubleheader
morning_brew: It is a massive Friday in the Hub, and my calendar has been circled for this back-to-back tilt at the Garden for a week. First up, we have the Bruins hosting the Maple Leafs in what is always a chippy affair, especially after that long scrap involving Tanner Jeannot earlier in the week. We need the boys to turn the page and get back in the win column after that loss to the Jets, because letting these division rivals walk out of our building with two points is something I just cannot stomach. If the Bruins can tighten up the defensive zone and play with some real desperation, maybe we can finally start stringing some wins together before the calendar flips to December.

Once the ice clears, it is time for the hardwood as the C's host Atlanta for a crucial NBA Cup group stage matchup. We are sitting at twelve and six and fighting for position in the Eastern Conference, so every win in this tournament matters more than the casual observer might think. I am looking for a focused effort from Jayson Tatum and the rest of the crew to keep this momentum steady, especially after we got back on track earlier this week. There is just something about these mid-season tournament games that brings out a different level of intensity, and I am ready to see if we can capitalize on home court advantage.

I am gonna be locked into both games from start to finish because that is just what we do in this town. Whether it is hockey or basketball, the energy at the Garden is always different when we get two Boston teams playing under the same roof on a Friday. I am not gonna make any big predictions because I do not wanna jinx anything, but I sure hope the beer is cold and the scoreboard is lopsided in our favor by the time the final buzzer sounds tonight. If Uncle Carmine tries to claim he watched every minute while he is snoring in the recliner during the third period, I am gonna lose it.

news_digest.headline: Celtics host Hawks Friday for NBA Cup group stage matchup
news_digest.dans_take: These NBA Cup games have a weird energy, but I am all in if it keeps the wins stacking up.

news_digest.headline: Maple Leafs take on the Bruins in Atlantic Division action
news_digest.dans_take: The Leafs could show up at the Garden with a choir and a box of chocolates and I would still want them sent home empty-handed.

trend_watch.trend: Tatum continues to anchor the Celtics offense as we look to build on our current record.
trend_watch.dans_take: The man is playing at an elite level and he is basically carrying the entire city on his back right now.

trend_watch.trend: Swayman is looking to bounce back in the crease after the tough result against Winnipeg.
trend_watch.dans_take: We need the real Swayman back in net because my heart cannot take another night of watching pucks slide past him.

trend_watch.trend: Jeannot is bringing the physical edge to the lineup after engaging in a lengthy fight.
trend_watch.dans_take: I love the grit, but let us hope he spends more time lighting the lamp than lighting up some Leafs' face today.
